plants.name: Hydrangea paniculata
plants.description: Tall cones of creamy-white blossoms rise from sturdy shrubs and slowly blush pink as late summer goes on. The flowers are lightly fragrant and draw butterflies and bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to September, so mid-August is peak bloom
plants.location: Gardens across Europe and temperate North America. The species is native to Japan, China and Sakhalin.
plants.funFact: Unlike the blue-and-pink mophead hydrangeas, panicle hydrangeas bloom on new growth. Late frosts rarely spoil their show, which is part of why they are so dependable.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. The flowers glow across sunny meadows, prairies and cottage borders in high summer, and goldfinches and butterflies visit them constantly.
plants.bloomingSeason: Roughly June to September, with peak flowering in July and August
plants.location: Prairies, open woodlands and gardens of central and eastern North America
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek word for hedgehog, a reference to the spiny central cone. Native peoples of the Great Plains used the plant medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family looks like a crown of silky, pink-tipped bracts around a downy center. In the Southern Hemisphere's winter it brightens the misty slopes of the Cape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, around June to October, so mid-August falls within it
plants.location: Fynbos shrublands of the Western Cape, South Africa, including the Kirstenbosch gardens
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It belongs to a plant family so ancient that it dates back to when the southern continents were joined as Gondwana.
